summary: The root حري primarily signifies being worthy or deserving of something, often implying a strong likelihood or fitness for it.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: حَرَى حر حران حرى حري حريي, aor. يَحْرِى, (S, K,) inf. n. حَرْىٌ, (S,) It (a thing S) decreased, diminished, or waned, (S, K, TA,) after increase; (TA;) as does, for instance, the moon. (S, TA.) [See an ex. in a verse cited in art. است.] حَرَى أَنْ يَكُونَ ٰلِكَ i. q. عَسَى [ May-be, or may-hap, &c., that will be ]. (TA.) حَرِىَ بِكَ َا He was, or became, adapted, disposed, apt, meet, suited, suitable, fitted, fit, competent, or proper, for such a thing; or worthy of it. (MA.) حَرَاهُ: see 5.

احراهُ احراه احراة أحر أحراه أحرى It (time) caused it (a thing, S) to decrease, diminish, or wane. (S, K.) مَا أَحْرَاهُ, and أَحْرِ بِهِ, How well adapted or disposed, or how apt, meet, suited, suitable, fitted, fit, competent, or proper, or how worthy, is he! (S, K.) [You say, مَا أَحْرَاهُ بِ ٰلِكَ How well adapted or disposed, &c., is he for that! ]

تحرّى أحرى حر حرى تحرى تحري signifies قَصَدَ الحَرَى; i. e. He sought, or repaired to, the vicinage, quarter, tract, or region, of a people: this is said to be the primary signification: (Mgh:) and تحرّاهُ he sought, or repaired to, his vicinage, &c.; ( قَصَدَ حَرَاهُ;) as also, aor. يَحْرِى: (TA:) he aimed at it; made it his object; sought, endeavoured after, pursued, or endeavoured to reach or attain or obtain, it; intended or purposed it; namely, a thing.

حَرًى حر حران حرى حري حريي The vicinage, quarter, tract, or region, (As, T, S, IAth, Mgh, K,) of a man, (As, T, IAth,) or of a people; (Mgh;) the environs (As, T, S) of a man, (As, T,) or of a house; (S;) and signifies the same: (S, K:) and [it is said that] the former signifies also the place of the eggs of an ostrich: (S, K:) and a covert, or hiding-place, among trees, of a gazelle: (K, * TA:) Lth says that it signifies the place of laying eggs of the ostrich; or the covert, or lodging-place,…
حَرٍ حر: see حَرِىٌّ, in four places.
حَرَاةٌ حر حراه حران حراة حرى: see حَرًى, in two places.

حَرِىٌّ حر حران حرى حري حريي Adapted, disposed, apt, meet, suited, suitable, fitted, fit, competent, proper, or worthy; as also and, which last has no dual nor pl., (S, Msb, K,) nor a fem. form, remaining unaltered, because it is [originally] an inf. n.; [see a verse cited voce نَقْرٌ;] or, accord. to Lh, one may say حَرَيَانِ, because Ks has related that some of the Arabs dualize what they do not pluralize: (TA:) the pl. of حَرِىٌّ is حَرِيُّونَ and أَحْرِيَآءُ; (S, Msb;) and the pl.
حِرِىٌّ حر حران حرى حري حريي: see art. حرح.

حَارٍ حار masc. of حَارِيَةٌ, (M, TA,) which is an epithet applied to a viper ( أَفْعًى ); (S, M, K;) meaning That has decreased in its body by reason of age; and it is the worst, or most malignant or noxious, that is: (S:) or that has become old, and has wasted in its body, and whereof there remains not save its head and its breath ( نَفَسُهَا [in the CK نَفْسُهَا ]) and its poison: (M, K:) dim..
حُوَيْرٍ حوير: see what next precedes.

أَحْرَى More, and most, adapted, disposed, apt, meet, suited, suitable, fitted, fit, competent, or proper; or more, and most, worthy, or deserving. (S, * Mgh, Msb, K.) A thing is said to be أَحْرَى بِٱلِاسْتِعْمَالِ [ More, or most, meet, &c., to be done ]. (S, K.)
مَحْرًى محر محرى محري محريي: see حَرِىٌّ.
مَحْرَاةٌ محر محراه محراة: see حَرِىٌّ, in two places.

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
